questions.question: At 20% per annum rate, an amount is doubled in approximately in ______ years at compound interest.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Rate (r) = 20% per annum

Amount becomes double ⇒ A = 2P

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculation:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + 20/100)t

⇒ 2 = (1.2)t

Now, take logarithm both sides:

⇒ log(2) = t × log(1.2)

⇒ t = log(2) ÷ log(1.2)

⇒ t = 0.3010 ÷ 0.0792

⇒ t ≈ 3.8 years

**∴ The amount is doubled in approximately 4 years.**

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum is ₹240. What is the principal lent?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum is ₹240.

**Formula Used:**

Difference between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) for 3 years = P × (r/100)³ + 3P × (r/100)²

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

Rate (r) = 20%

Time (t) = 3 years

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years = ₹240

⇒ P × (20/100)³ + 3P × (20/100)² = 240

⇒ P × (0.2)³ + 3P × (0.2)² = 240

⇒ P × 0.008 + 3P × 0.04 = 240

⇒ 0.008P + 0.12P = 240

⇒ 0.128P = 240

⇒ P = 240 / 0.128

⇒ P = 1875

**The principal lent is ₹1,875.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹56

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹58

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = P × ((1 + R ÷ 100)² - 1)

**Calculation:**

56 = (P × R × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ P × R = 2800

From CI formula:

58 = P × ((1 + R ÷ 100)² - 1)

Substitute R = 2800 ÷ P from the first equation:

⇒ 58 = P × ((1 + (2800 ÷ P ÷ 100))² - 1)

⇒ 58 = P × ((1 + (28 ÷ P))² - 1)

Expanding the equation:

⇒ 58 = P × (1 + 56 ÷ P + 784 ÷ P² - 1)

⇒ 58 = P × (56 ÷ P + 784 ÷ P²)

⇒ 58 = 56 + (784 ÷ P)

⇒ 784 ÷ P = 58 - 56

⇒ 784 ÷ P = 2

⇒ P = 784 ÷ 2

⇒ P = ₹392

**∴ The principal is ₹392.**

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹60 and compound interest is ₹64, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a period of 2 years, the Principal can be calculated directly using the relationship between CI and SI:

Principal (P) = (SI ÷ 2)² ÷ (CI − SI)

⇒ P = (60 ÷ 2)² ÷ (64 − 60)

⇒ P = 30² ÷ 4 = 900 ÷ 4 = 225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹60

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹64

Time (T) = 2 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b0722c52d72712ccb3be7fdcb8ac86ce7f429f542cba5ce53a13cfea16cc65c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 1 year = 60 ÷ 2 = ₹30

⇒ The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is simply the interest generated on the 1st year's SI.

⇒ Difference = CI − SI = 64 − 60 = ₹4

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest on SI × 100) ÷ SI for 1st year

⇒ R = (4 × 100) ÷ 30 = 40/3 %

⇒ Now, substituting the values in the 1-year SI formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 30 = (P × 40/3 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 30 = (P × 40) ÷ 300

⇒ P = (30 × 300) ÷ 40 = 9000 ÷ 40 = 225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The formula is: Difference = P × (R / 100)², which effectively equals the interest earned on the first year's simple interest.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The formula for 3 years is: Difference = P × (R / 100)² × (3 + R / 100).

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple interest is charged entirely on the base principal amount, whereas compound interest is charged on the principal as well as any accumulated interest from previous periods (interest on interest).

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 12 years when the interest is compounded annually. In how many more years will it become eight times of itself?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **x** times in **T** years at compound interest, it becomes **xⁿ** times in **nT** years.

The sum becomes 2 times (x = 2) in 12 years (T = 12).

To become 8 times, we need it to become 2³ times (n = 3).

Total time to become 8 times = 12 × 3 = 36 years.

More years required = Total time − Time already elapsed = 36 − 12 = 24 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

questions.question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 5.5% and 6.5% per annum, respectively. Ramesh borrowed an amount of ₹3,00,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Ramesh after 2 years.

Loan amount from Bank A = ₹3,00,000

Loan amount from Bank B = ₹3,00,000

Interest rate from Bank B = 6.5% per annum

SI from Bank B:

**The positive difference between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Ramesh after 2 years is ₹6,000.**
